outcome: One unified storage and virtualisation platform for clinical systems, commissioned and validated together instead of bolted on afterwards.
overview: A leading hospital in India needed reliable unified storage and virtualisation for its clinical systems, and Redington implemented rack servers with Unity XT unified storage and VMware. The shape of that engagement is worth recording because it is the common one, and the least written about: not a transformation programme, but a dependable platform for the systems clinicians use all day, delivered so that the storage and virtualisation layers are commissioned together against one acceptance test rather than procured separately and integrated afterwards, under time pressure, by whoever is left holding both. That sequencing is what this record is really about.

benefits.text: Block and file are served from one unified platform rather than two separate systems
benefits.limits: The published reference describes one named customer engagement. It is evidence that Redington has delivered this, and it is not a performance figure that transfers to the next customer

benefits.text: Storage and virtualisation are commissioned together as one validated platform
benefits.limits: Joint commissioning reduces integration risk; it does not remove the need for clinical system vendors to validate their own applications on it

benefits.text: Storage remains portable across vendors at the next refresh because the protocols are standard
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance data; a design built on invoice history or on projected growth alone produces a quotation rather than an architecture

residency: Clinical data remains on hospital-owned equipment in the hospital data centre

notFor.situation: A hospital with a current, supported storage and virtualisation platform
notFor.why: Replacement without a support, capacity or performance driver is change for its own sake

notFor.situation: An estate large enough to need scale-out unstructured storage for imaging
notFor.why: Unified primary storage and a petabyte-scale imaging archive are different design points

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Dell implementation partner; the referenced engagement was delivered by Redington with Dell · Duration: 10–14 weeks to a commissioned platform with clinical systems migrated, hardware lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor hardware and software support with a replacement term matched to clinical criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor cases across compute, storage and virtualisation.
1) Assessment — capacity, measured performance, clinical vendor constraints and downtime tolerances
2) Design — sizing, platform layout, migration order and rollback plan
3) Build and commission — servers, storage and virtualisation commissioned and validated as one platform
4) Migrate and hand over — clinical systems migrated within tolerance, operations handed over
deliverables: The platform passes one joint commissioning test covering compute, storage and virtualisation together
Every clinical migration completes within its agreed downtime tolerance or is rolled back inside it
Measured performance for clinical systems meets the design figure
effort: 10–14 weeks to a commissioned platform with clinical systems migrated, hardware lead time excluded
